Spec review companion · #107 · snapshot c27e4b4 · 2026-10-27

Split Copilot JSON events at LF only

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #107

The change

A review or task fails with "Failed to parse Copilot JSON output" when Copilot's output holds a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside a JSON string. The companion read the output with readline, which also ends a line at those two characters, so one event arrived in pieces. assessment:29

The fix splits the output at LF only, with one CR before it dropped, in a chunk buffer shaped like upstream's handleChunk. fix:10

9files changed fix:18
11tests added fix:56
6checks passed, 0 failed test:19
5deviations, all from the review rounds fix:76

Root cause

readline treats U+2028 and U+2029 as line ends. JSON allows both raw inside a string, and Copilot leaves them raw. The first piece that does not parse ends the run. Confidence high: reproduced. assessment:51

Remediation

A per-client buffer: cut at each LF, drop one CR, pass each line to the unchanged handleLine. A last line with no LF is read at stdout end. Output after the run has finished is ignored. assessment:58

What moved since you last read it

Review round 4 changed only the tests. assessment.md and the reader did not change.

How it works

Examples

These are the cases the tests run, as recorded in the bug notes. Nothing was run to build this page.

Raw U+2028 in an answer

Expected: one assistant.message with the exact text, exit 0. This is the reported failure. assessment:83

A lone CR between two events

Expected: the quoting parse error. Proves that only LF splits, and fails on the old reader. assessment:86 fix:71

CRLF line ends

Expected: every event parses, no CR stays. Copilot on Windows may write CRLF. assessment:84

Output after the run

A stop that fails finishes the run while stdout is open. Expected: no event, no result, the timeout error kept. assessment:88

A result line with no LF

Expected: the result is kept, as readline kept it. A not-JSON last line still fails with the quoting error. assessment:87

  2. The lone-CR difference from readline. A lone CR no longer ends a line. Check that this is acceptable for Copilot's output. test:41 assessment:62

The assessment defers nothing on purpose; it has no open questions. assessment:106

Look-ups

Glossary
  • U+2028, U+2029: the Unicode line separator and paragraph separator. JSON allows them raw inside a string.
  • LF, CR: line feed and carriage return, the line ends of JSON-lines output.
  • handleChunk: upstream's buffer that cuts a stream at LF, which the fix copies in shape.

# Bug Assessment: Copilot JSON events with U+2028 or U+2029 are split and fail to parse - **Slug**: 107-split-events-at-lf-only- **Created**: 2026-10-26- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #107)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: high ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Summarized from #107. The companion reads Copilot's JSON events with `node:readline`(`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs:198`). `readline` ends a line at U+2028 (lineseparator) and U+2029 (paragraph separator), as well as at LF and CR. JSON allows both charactersunescaped inside a string, so Copilot can print an event that holds one. The companion then gets theevent in pieces, and none of them parses. Seen on 2026-10-20 in #105, review round 16: ```Copilot error: Failed to parse Copilot JSON output: Unterminated string in JSON at position 1832 (line 1 column 1833){"type":"tool.execution_complete", ... "result":{"content":"...``` Expected: an event line splits only at LF (a CR before it is dropped); a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside aJSON string stays in the event, and the run goes on. The issue asks for the chunk buffer ofupstream's `handleChunk`, the same event handling otherwise (also the error that quotes a line that isnot JSON), and the two separators in the fake and in `tests/prompt-mode.test.mjs`. ## Symptom Any review or task fails with "Failed to parse Copilot JSON output" when Copilot reads, quotes orwrites text that holds a raw U+2028 or U+2029, for example a file copied from a web page or a Worddocument. Expected: the event is read whole and the run goes on. ## Reproduction 1. Write one valid JSON event line whose string holds a raw U+2028 and U+2029, for example   `JSON.stringify({ type: "assistant.message", data: { content: "a" + String.fromCharCode(0x2028) + "b" + String.fromCharCode(0x2029) + "c" } })`   (`JSON.stringify` does not escape them), followed by LF.2. Feed it to `readline.createInterface` on a stream, as `prompt-mode.mjs` does.3. Checked on 2026-10-26 with Node 24.21.0: 3 `line` events, and `JSON.parse` fails on all 3.   `JSON.parse` of the whole line works. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs:198-201` — `readline.createInterface({ input: this.proc.stdout })` and its `line` handler split stdout into events; readline also ends lines at U+2028 and U+2029.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs:218-230` (`handleLine`) — gets each piece and sets `protocolError` with "Failed to parse Copilot JSON output" on the first piece that does not parse.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs` `finish()` — closes `this.readline`.- Upstream `plugins/codex/scripts/lib/app-server.mjs:220` reads its spawned client the same way; its broker path (`handleChunk`, lines 107-116) already splits at LF only. ## Root Cause Hypothesis `node:readline` treats U+2028 and U+2029 as line ends, but they are valid unescaped characters in aJSON string, and Copilot's JSON-lines output (like `JSON.stringify`) leaves them raw. So one eventreaches `handleLine` as several pieces, and the first piece that fails to parse ends the run.Confidence: high (reproduced). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: replace `readline` with the chunk buffer of upstream's `handleChunk`: append eachstdout chunk (stdout is already decoded as UTF-8) to a buffer, cut it at each LF, drop one CR beforethe LF, and pass each line to the unchanged `handleLine`. When stdout ends, pass the rest of thebuffer (a last line with no LF) to `handleLine`, as readline did, so a cut-off or not-JSON last lineis still reported. Remove the `readline` import and the `readline.close()` in `finish()`. Outputthat arrives after `finish()` (possible when a stop fails and `finish()` runs before stdout ends) isignored: the `data` and `end` handlers return at once once the run has exited, so late output cannotdispatch an event, change the result or start a result timer. A lone CR no longer ends a line(readline split there too); the issue asks for LF only, and JSON-lines output from Copilot ends eachrecord with LF. This difference is part of the README entry. **Alternatives**:- Keep readline and join pieces after a failed parse: fragile, and it could change the error that  quotes a line that is not JSON. Rejected.- `crlfDelay` and other readline options cannot turn off the Unicode line ends. **Files likely to change**:- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs`- `tests/fake-copilot-fixture.mjs` (an env switch that ends event lines with CRLF, added to the fake's list of passed variables next to `FAKE_COPILOT_ANSWER`; the separators already pass through `FAKE_COPILOT_ANSWER`)- `tests/prompt-mode.test.mjs` (the chunk, late-output and partial-line cases use small inline scripts, as its existing stop tests do, because the fake writes each event in one `write`)- No other doc: no doc names readline; `specs/005-copilot-plugin-port/call-site-map.md` maps `handleLine` and `handleChunk` to upstream and stays true (and is history)- `README.md` "Differences from the Codex plugin" (a correctness difference from upstream)- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (patch release) **Tests to add or update**:- An answer with a raw U+2028, and one with a raw U+2029: one `assistant.message` event with the exact text, no `protocolError`, the result kept, exit 0.- CRLF line ends: every event parses and no text ends with `\r`.- An event cut across two stdout chunks, two events in one chunk, and a CR and its LF in separate chunks (the buffer joins and splits them).- Two JSON objects separated by a lone CR are one line: the run fails with the quoting error (only LF splits).- A last line with no LF is still read: a valid event is dispatched, and a not-JSON last line fails with the quoting error, also when the process exits at once.- Output after the run has finished (and after a `protocolError`) dispatches no event and leaves the result and the error as they are.- A run that times out with a partial line in the buffer keeps its timeout error.- One event of more than 1 MB, written in many chunks, is read whole.- The existing "a line that is not JSON ends the run with an error that quotes it" test stays as it is.- In test source, the separators are written as `String.fromCharCode(0x2028)` and `0x2029`, not as raw characters, so the files stay readable for tools that read them line by line. ## Risks & Considerations - A multi-byte UTF-8 character cut across two chunks: `setEncoding("utf8")` on stdout already  decodes across chunk ends, so the buffer sees whole characters.- Order of the last `data`, `end` and the process `close`: `close` fires after stdio has closed, so the  flush on stdout `end` runs before `finish()`. The flush must not run after `finish()` or after a  `protocolError` (`handleLine` already returns at once on a `protocolError`).- A very long event line stays in memory until its LF, as with readline.- Upstream has the same defect; the owner reports it upstream ("Tickets", Upstream). ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. The module and function names stay; the reader takes the shape of  upstream's own `handleChunk`. The change from upstream's `readline` reader is a correctness  difference, listed in the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" with its reason.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. Code written here, after upstream's `handleChunk`; no new  dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. Still the documented JSON output, one  record per line; the adapter boundary does not change.- **IV. Safe by default**: met. No change to permissions, the read-only rule or how Copilot starts.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. LF splitting with one CR dropped works the same on every OS; CRLF is  tested.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Tests for both separators, CRLF, split and joined  chunks, the last line with no LF, and the existing not-JSON error. Patch release with its  `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the release run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: Copilot JSON events with U+2028 or U+2029 are split and fail to parse - **Slug**: 107-split-events-at-lf-only- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary The companion now splits Copilot's stdout into event lines at LF only, with one CR before itdropped, through a chunk buffer in the shape of upstream's `handleChunk`, instead of `readline`,which also ended lines at U+2028 and U+2029. Output after the run has finished is ignored. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/prompt-mode.mjs` | modified | `readline` removed; `handleChunk` splits at LF, searches only the new chunk, joins a line's pieces once, drops one CR, and reads nothing once the run has exited or after a protocol error (it also stops in the middle of a chunk); stdout `end` passes a last line with no LF through `handleChunk` || `tests/fake-copilot-fixture.mjs` | modified | `FAKE_COPILOT_CRLF` ends each event line with CRLF; added to the variables the fake reads from the test, not the outer environment || `tests/prompt-mode.test.mjs` | added tests | separators, CRLF, chunks, a separator cut inside its bytes across pipe chunks, lone CR, last line with no LF, timeout with a partial line, output after the run, output after a protocol error, an event over 1 MB; `startFake` takes extra env || `README.md` | modified | "Differences from the Codex plugin": the LF-only split, with its reason || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.19` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | version 1.0.19 (`npm run bump-version`) | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jshandleChunk(chunk) {  if (this.exited || this.protocolError) {    return;  }  let start = 0;  let newlineIndex = chunk.indexOf("\n");  while (newlineIndex !== -1) {    this.lineParts.push(chunk.slice(start, newlineIndex));    const line = this.lineParts.join("");    this.lineParts = [];    start = newlineIndex + 1;    this.handleLine(line.endsWith("\r") ? line.slice(0, -1) : line);    if (this.protocolError) {      return;    }    newlineIndex = chunk.indexOf("\n", start);  }  if (start < chunk.length) {    this.lineParts.push(chunk.slice(start));  }}``` At stdout end, a non-empty `lineParts` is passed through `handleChunk("\n")`, so the last line takesthe same CR rule. ## Tests Added or Updated - `tests/prompt-mode.test.mjs` "an event whose JSON string holds a raw U+2028 is read as one event" and the U+2029 case — the bug; both fail on the old reader.- "CRLF line ends are read, and no CR stays in the events" — CRLF from Copilot still works.- "events are joined across chunks and split within one, also with CR and LF in separate chunks" — gives the exact chunks to `handleChunk`, also an event cut inside its U+2028.- "a lone CR does not end a line, so two events joined by it fail with the quoting error" — only LF splits (fails on the old reader, which split at the CR).- "a last line with no LF is still read: a result is kept, and text that is not JSON fails".- "a run that times out with part of a line kept keeps its timeout error".- "output after the run has finished changes nothing" — after a result and a stop that fails, a late result given to `handleChunk` does not replace it.- "output after a protocol error is not read, also in the same chunk" — no event, no result, nothing kept in `lineParts`.- "a separator cut inside its UTF-8 bytes across two pipe chunks is read whole".- "an event of more than 1 MB, written in many chunks, is read whole".- The existing "a line that is not JSON ends the run with an error that quotes it" is unchanged and passes. ## Local Verification - Commands run: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build` → pass; `npm test` → 422 tests, 398 pass, 24 skipped, 0 fail (after review round 2: 423 tests, 399 pass); `npm run check-version` → 1.0.19; `claude plugin validate .` → pass.- Against the old `prompt-mode.mjs` (the fix taken out for one run, before the review rounds): the U+2028, U+2029 and lone-CR tests fail; the others then passed. The tests added in the review rounds that call `handleChunk` directly cannot run on the old reader (it has no `handleChunk`), and the byte-split test fails on it like the other separator tests.- Manual check: a one-line script fed one JSON event with both separators to `readline` and got 3 line events, none of which parsed (Node 24.21.0). ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27, review round 1 (`code-review`): the buffer keeps the pieces of a line in a list,  searches only the new chunk for LF and joins the pieces once per line, so a large event no longer  costs time that grows with the square of its size; it also stops reading after a protocol error;  the stdout `end` flush passes the rest through `handleChunk`, so the CR rule lives in one place.  The assessment's shape (cut at LF, drop one CR, flush the last line, ignore output after the run)  is unchanged.- 2026-10-27, review round 1: the late-output test now gives the chunk to `handleChunk` directly.  A stop that fails closes the child's pipes (`releaseChild`), so late output cannot arrive through  the pipe; the guard is kept for the case the assessment names. The chunk-split test also calls  `handleChunk` directly, because a pipe may join writes that come close together.- 2026-10-27, review round 2 (`code-review`): after a protocol error, `handleChunk` also stops in the  middle of a chunk and keeps no partial line. The late-output test now uses a case that only the  exited guard covers (a Copilot that stays alive after its result and cannot be stopped; any stop  that fails before a protocol error is another), and  the protocol-error test puts the error and a partial line in one chunk; with the guard taken out,  the late-output test fails. A new test cuts a U+2028 inside its UTF-8 bytes across two pipe  chunks.- 2026-10-27, review round 3 (`code-review`): the protocol-error check inside `handleChunk` is one  return right after `handleLine`, in place of checks in the loop condition and before the last  push; the behaviour is the same. The late-output test stops its stand-in Copilot in `t.after`, so  a failed assertion leaves no process running.- 2026-10-27, review round 4 (`code-review`): every test that starts a stand-in Copilot that never  exits stops it in `t.after`, so a failure there cannot leave `npm test` waiting. ## Follow-ups - Upstream codex-plugin-cc reads its app server with `readline` too; the owner reports it upstream.
